title: Priority-aware batch allocator for streaming chat
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a priority-aware batch formation heuristic for streaming chat completions that balances low tail latency for high-priority traffic, KV cache locality for ongoing conversations, and worst-case GPU memory boundedness. This ticket covers allocator design, integration with the continuous batching loop, KV cache pinning/eviction signals, and a conservative rollout plan.
updates: 2026-02-10: Initial ticket created — scope scoped to allocator and KV signals only; not touching global scheduler yet.

2026-02-11: Spike completed — microbenchmarked simple priority-first queue vs. time-window-first. Priority-first reduced p99 for <10k token priority streams by ~18% but increased some multi-turn KV misses.
2026-02-13: Design doc posted to Confluence with allocator state machine and memory budget rules (link below). Chose hybrid heuristic: priority watermark + adaptive micro-window.

2026-02-15: Prototype landed: priority watermark that lets up to N high-priority streams preempt a current low-priority batch if preemption budget allows. Also added per-batch estimated memory budget enforcement.

2026-02-17: Integration with KV cache controller: allocator now emits 'pin' hints for streams likely to continue; KV controller accepts pin hints and delays eviction. Observed GPU memory diffusion reduced by ~12% during soak tests.

2026-02-18: Running extended perf job against canary cluster; observed 3% throughput decrease but 11% p99 latency improvement for priority traffic. Next: tune allocation thresholds and add fallback policies for extreme memory pressure.
acceptance_criteria: 1) High-priority streaming requests (label=priority:high) see p99 generation latency reduced by >=10% vs baseline under mixed load
2) Overall token throughput drop <= 5% at target load compared to baseline batching policy
3) No increased OOM incidents in canary cluster after 48h soak (monitored by gpu-oom-alerts)
4) KV cache hit rate for pinned conversation prefixes improves or stays within 2% of baseline for long-lived streams
5) Rollout runbook and automatic fallback to time-window policy implemented and tested in chaos scenarios
testing_plan: Unit tests for allocator decision logic (priority preemption, micro-window expiry, memory budget check)
Integration test: end-to-end synthetic workload with mixed priorities and long-lived streams verifying KV pin/unpin signaling
Soak test: 48h canary with 3 instance types (A100-40G, A10G, T4) capturing p50/p95/p99, gpu mem, and cache hit-rate
Fault injection: simulate KV controller rejecting pins and verify allocator falls back to non-pinning policy without OOM
Load regression: ensure tokens/sec drop is within acceptable bounds under expected peak traffic profile
notes: Design decisions summary: Adopt hybrid heuristic — keep a small adaptive micro-window (default 12ms) to aggregate similar-latency requests, but allow a high-priority watermark to preempt for up to M tokens worth of preemption budget per scheduling epoch.

KV policy: pin hints are soft — KV controller can decline during memory pressure. When pin accepted, allocator reserves small KV budget slice and increases batch affinity score for that stream for the next K steps.

Memory budgeting: Use per-GPU transient budget. Each batch estimates required working set (model activations + kv cache delta) using a lightweight estimator and refuses to grow beyond a configurable fraction (default 75%) of usable device memory.
Compression: Prototype leverages 8-bit compressed KV snapshots for long-lived low-priority streams when GPU memory pressure is high; this sacrifices some cache hit quality for memory safety.
Fallbacks: If the allocator detects sustained OOM or >3% GPU memory reclaim events in a minute, it flips to conservative time-window batching and disables preemption for 1 minute.
Instrumentation: Emit batch_id, batch_size, preemption_count, estimated_batch_memory, kv_pins_accepted to tracing to correlate perf regressions with allocator decisions.
Open questions: optimal default values for micro-window (12ms) and preemption token budget; need product input on acceptable throughput vs. latency tradeoffs for P1 customers.
